definitions.explanation: Used to add information that strengthens or supplements what was said before.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}い。しかも{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: This restaurant is cheap. Moreover, it's delicious.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{頭|あたま}がいい。しかも{努力家|どりょくか}だ。
examples.english: He's smart. What's more, he's hardworking.

examples.japanese: {遅刻|ちこく}した。しかも{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}に。
examples.english: I was late. And it was to an important meeting.

notes:
USAGE: しかも adds emphasis to additional information. It typically introduces something surprising or noteworthy that reinforces the previous statement.

CONTRAST:
・しかも - moreover (adds emphasis, often positive or surprising)
・その{上|うえ} - on top of that, moreover
・{更|さら}に - furthermore, even more
・おまけに - on top of that (often negative additional point)

POSITION: Typically appears at the beginning of a new sentence or clause.
